questions.question: What characterises a visual learner?
options: They learn best by seeing - pictures, diagrams, colours and videos
They learn best by listening to podcasts
They learn best through physical activities
They cannot learn languages
questions.explanation: Visual learners learn best by seeing. Auditory learners learn by hearing, and kinaesthetic learners by doing.

questions.question: Which strategy fits an auditory learner best?
options: Listening to English podcasts and reading texts aloud
Drawing mind maps with colours
Building physical models
Avoiding all sound while studying
questions.explanation: Auditory learners learn best by hearing - podcasts, audiobooks, discussions and reading aloud work well for them.

questions.question: What is the "context method" for learning new words?
options: Learning words by meeting them in real texts and situations, not just word lists
Memorising the dictionary page by page
Only learning words that look like Norwegian words
Skipping all unknown words
questions.explanation: Learning words in context - through reading and listening - helps you remember them better and learn how they are actually used.

questions.question: How can flashcards help you learn vocabulary?
options: They let you test yourself repeatedly, which strengthens your memory
They do your homework automatically
They translate texts for you
They only work for maths
questions.explanation: Flashcards use active recall - testing yourself repeatedly - which is one of the most effective ways to memorise vocabulary.

questions.question: Most people learn best by:
options: Using a mix of several learning styles
Using only one learning style their whole life
Never changing their study methods
Avoiding strategies altogether
questions.explanation: Most people use a combination of visual, auditory, kinaesthetic and reading/writing strategies - mixing methods usually works best.
